text: What if Photoshop were rebuilt from scratch in Rust and every editing command could also
be driven by an AI agent? That’s PhotoCraft, an open-source, clean-room image editor with
a native egui interface and a GPU compositor built on wgpu. It already supports layered
PSD files, adjustment layers, masks, type, brushes, smart objects, smart filters, and
local subject and object selection. But the unusual part is the architecture. Every
action is a command, so the same editing engine can be controlled from the desktop UI,
CLI, JSON, or an MCP server. The project even tracks Photoshop’s menu tree and
currently reports all 627 menu items wired to live commands. That does not mean
full Photoshop parity yet. PhotoCraft still calls itself early alpha, and its
roadmap says fidelity and deeper behavior remain unfinished. Still, it’s a
fascinating look at what an agent-ready creative app can look like.
